item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Verillion! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. It's nice to see the off-site fanbase make their way onto the official site for this little project. I can very much see why made-up scenarios keep you awake at night - after all, this site is all about it, isn't it? I really can't wait to see what kinds of writings you'll put on the site for us to enjoy!

Without further ado, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

Hi there, this is me, Lesk, and I've joined the site (after 2 years of having a friend endlessly explain me stuff about scps over and over) after taking some glances around many entries, and I've thought that maybe becoming part of this and getting my tries 'round writing some entries/stories would help me become a better writer and not totally use this as a way to train myself for an oncoming english test to develop better writing techniques.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi everyone!

I love creative stories and heard about the SCP a few months ago. After looking at the site and reading both old and new articles, I can see that this is something really special. In a way, the stories here give me the same sense of awe and wonder I get when reading about ancient Egyptian or Greek mythology, except with a special 21st-century internet twist. I have an idea or two for an SCP article, and it would be an honor to have it accepted someday (after many, many rounds of feedback and rewrites of course:))

One thing that keeps me up at night is probably the inner workings of how we communicate. Language is so complex, yet I sometimes find myself struggling to find how best to phrase an idea or viewpoint.

I'm very excited to be a part of this community, and I hope I'll get to know many of you as we add to this pantheon of the 21st century!

Hello, I am an author interested in adding an SCP to the site sometime in the near future. I've known about the foundation for around 2-3 years but I've just recently (past 3-4 months) started to really get into it. I hope that sometime in the near future I can add an SCP that many can enjoy.

As for the random question, there are a couple things that keep me up at night. The most common are made up scenarios, often involving putting myself in a characters shoes from a book or show that I enjoy. Otherwise, its thoughts of the past and what could have been.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
How is everyone doing?

My name is Joel.

Anyways, why am I here? Well, you can probably thank the Youtube video blogger Ekhert's Ladder for that. I was watching one of his videos, and found myself here, obsessively reading entries. Some have been better than others, but there have been others that have been inspiring, creative, and even downright iconic (SCP-682, what I call The Plot Armor Reptile, SCP-1342, or what I call: What NOT to do to your Closest, Possibly Only Ally, SCP-1000 Bigfoot, SCP-2273, or what I call YOU MANIACS and YOU BLEW IT UP!!!, etc.).

As someone who loves themes that explores extraterrestrial life, alternate universe, running gags (again, SCP-682), and more emotional themes, such as hope and fear, and cruelty and morality (Foundation seems to be somewhat lacking in far the latter, and has ample amounts of in the one before that), the SCP multiverse is a fascinating medium for exploring such concepts. And yes, I'm a huge nerd, who will without hesitation make TV culture references.

I hope to write one or two entries, since it isn't like I don't have at least one idea for an SCP. As for whether or not I actually complete it is another matter, since I have hobbies in drawing/Photoshop/Illustrator, and more than occasionally in video games, and hope to go back to school, and begin a major Political Science next season. Not to mention I'd need to stop reading entries long enough to write something of substance!

Don't expect me to write any stories of gore and dark creatures in darkened hallways here to steal the souls of any Mobile Task Forces foolish enough to try to capture him, and disembowel any researcher foolish enough to refer to him by "it" or "SCP" though. Do expect content like an alternate instance of SCP-682 getting a cameo, and being dragged out, kicking, screaming, and shouting threats to something that doesn't consider it welcome. Because that is my sense of humor.

The only thing that seems to keep me up at night is on nights where I know that I have to get up early in the morning, but my brain won't SHUT DOWN ALREADY! Oddly enough, knowing that my part time job isn't enough to afford to move out, and that it will take at least two years to do something about it does not keep me up, even though it probably should.

item.content:encoded:
Hello, everybody. I guess call me Ainulindale (Ay-noo-LIN-duh-lay). I've been reading "The Silmarillion" and since character names are difficult to obtain as a user id, I went with the name of the first story. I just discovered SCP by accident and it was exactly what I needed to find but didn't know I was looking for.

While watching youtube videos about different gods/angels/esoteric writings (Nag Hammadi library, for example) and a video called something like "SCPs that could end the world" was in the suggestion list. When I googled SCP, I saw what it was and immediately became excited. I've been published, but I pretty much stopped a while ago. I feel that working to write for the SCP Foundation will help me hone my writing skills once more. I'm still familiarizing myself with the SCP universe but I will eventually contribute. I want to do it right though and will be looking to you all for guidance. Thanks for making and maintaining such a great project!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Do you remember, the twenty-first night of September… oh wait wrong month.

Hello everyone! My name is Morgane, I am 25 years old, I live in France.

I first came across the SCP Foundation wiki three or four years ago, I think. I don't remember how I arrived here (I often find things through clicking on links at half-random, following the flow of my mind.) I joined the French branch in 2017 but didn't do anything there, save from opening a (quite empty) Sandbox.

I have regained interest in the SCP Foundation wiki quite recently, and I thought I may enjoy giving a comment or two, or maybe even trying to write one idea I have for a SCP article (if I ever have the energy to do so), so I decided to join the main site.

I currently have no hobbies due to depression problems, but once I feel better, I intend to pursue my former hobbies: doodling, learning to play the piano, composing music, imagining a fictional language and a fictional country… Something I still keep doing, however, is reading webcomics.

Things that keep me up at night? Loneliness, trauma, and the aforementioned depression. To ignore them, I spend a lot of time on the internet, resulting in short nights. Ha!

I am happy to join this corner of the Internet.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hey there guys, hope you're doing well. Guess I'll introduce myself. When I was younger I loved reading, but for some reason I dropped it along the way. The SCP foundation gave me the chance to rediscover my old passion (and the stuff here certainly is better than those old child books). I've been a long time reader (maybe 2 years?), and due to not-so-good circumstances in my life I thought it would be nice to test myself as a writer, develop new skills and overall improve as a person trough something I really enjoy. Aside from that, there's not much else to say. My life mostly consist of studying, listening to weird music and playing my guitar. Also, English is not my native language so please excuse me if what I write seems messy. I hope we can all coexist and contribute to the wiki in a positive way!

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing! Take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!
